class.name: JarErodedTerrainSdf
class.brief_description: Terrain or planet with an erosion filter: branching gullies and sharp ridges, computed per point.
class.description: Displaces a flat ground plane ([constant SHAPE_FLAT], along +Y) or a sphere ([constant SHAPE_SPHERE]) by [member noise] scaled by [member height], then applies an erosion filter on top. The filter adds octaves of gullies that run down the slopes, branch, and fade out on peaks and in valleys. No simulation is involved: every point is evaluated on its own, so it works with chunked, infinite and editable volumes. The erosion technique is by Rune Skovbo Johansen (runevision), building on work by Clay John and Felix Westin (Fewes): [url=https://blog.runevision.com/2026/03/fast-and-gorgeous-erosion-filter.html]Fast and Gorgeous Erosion Filter[/url]. This is an independent implementation written from that article, extended to 3D cells so it also works on spheres. Surface nets suit eroded terrain best. Keep the smallest gullies ([member erosion_scale] / [member lacunarity]^([member octaves] - 1)) at least a few voxels wide; anything finer only aliases.

method.name: sample_height
method.description: Returns the eroded height above the base plane (or above the sphere of [member radius]) below or above [param position]. Useful for placing objects on the surface.

members.member: Gully directions follow the input slope, but the filter acts as if the input always had this steepness, because the eroded output is roughly equally steep everywhere. The input slope also decides where gullies appear: input that is much flatter than this (peaks and valleys) gets none.
How far smaller gullies reach onto flatter ground. Higher values add more fine gullies.
Width of the largest gullies, in meters.
Slope that each octave of gullies adds (rise over run). [code]0[/code] disables the erosion.
Amplitude factor from one octave to the next. With [code]gain = 1 / lacunarity[/code] every octave adds the same slope.
Weight of the gullies against the fade towards peaks and valleys. The strength is scaled by the inverse, so values below [code]1[/code] keep peaks pointy and ridges sharp.
Height of the base [member noise], in meters.
Width factor from one octave of gullies to the next: each octave is this many times narrower.
Base noise. Sampled in 2D (XZ) for [constant SHAPE_FLAT] and in 3D on the sphere for [constant SHAPE_SPHERE]. Without noise the base surface is flat and nothing erodes.
Number of gully octaves, from [member erosion_scale] down.
Radius of the base sphere for [constant SHAPE_SPHERE], in meters.

constants.constant: A heightfield along +Y, infinite in X and Z.
A planet of [member radius] around the origin.
